question: R3 control: recount Q from the plan and a Monte Carlo of the birthday law that fixes it
number: Recount: sqrt(2 N lambda) = 0.996995486 x 2^128 (lambda 0.497, success 0.39165), plus 28 L in flight (0.001709), over (1 - 1.5e-4): Q = 7B = 0.998854299 x 2^128, equal to the ledger. The plain-birthday value in B3R3-G1, 0.9943, is the same law at success exactly 0.39 (lambda 0.4943). Monte Carlo control, N = 2^32, 3,000 trials each: U = 0.9970 sqrtN: observed 0.3967 against the law 0.3916 (z 0.56); U = 0.8973 sqrtN: 0.3170 vs 0.3314 (z -1.67); U = 1.0967 sqrtN: 0.4383 vs 0.4519 (z -1.50).
notes: universe cell blake3-r3|LEDGER.EVALS|LEDGER|R3. The Monte Carlo is of independent uniform draws (the premise), not of the 3-round function; the function-level checks are T1-T3 and the metered runs in LEDGER.CTRL R3 / PREM.H2 R3. Two of three z values are near -1.6: no evidence of a bias in the law, but not a tight test either.
held_fixed: lambda 0.497; 28 L in flight; 1.5e-4 cut allowance; N = 2^256
